column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“He does not uncover my ear” is rendered “without disclosing it to me,” and “there is not this” as “It is not so!”
“Swore an oath” is rendered “vowed”; “about a step” becomes “hardly a step.”
“Whatever your soul says” is rendered “Whatever you say.”
“I will certainly sit” is rendered “I ought to sit down.”
“The sacrifice of the days” is rendered “the yearly sacrifice,” and “clan” as “family.”
“If it certainly burns to him” is rendered “if he is very angry.”
“Covenant loyalty” (Hebrew חֶסֶד) is rendered “deal kindly”; NASB adds “Therefore.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Who will tell me, or what if your father answers you harshly?” is condensed to “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “be witness!” after the divine name; the Hebrew oath is incomplete. “Uncover your ear” is rendered “make it known to you.”
NASB moves the condition “If it please my father to do you harm” to the front; “uncover your ear” becomes “make it known.”
“Covenant loyalty of the LORD” is rendered “the lovingkindness of the LORD.” The Hebrew sentence is difficult and the meaning is uncertain.
“Covenant loyalty” is rendered “lovingkindness.”
NASB supplies “a covenant” and “saying,” and renders the verb as a wish (“May the LORD require it”).
“The love of his own soul” is rendered “as he loved his own life.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“You will do three times” is rendered “When you have stayed for three days,” and “the day of the deed” as “that eventful day.” The meaning is uncertain.
“To send them for myself to a target” is rendered “as though I shot at a target.”
“There is not anything” is rendered “no harm.”
Close to the Hebrew; “young man” is rendered “youth.”
“The matter” is rendered “the agreement.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“As time on time” is rendered “as usual.” The Hebrew reads “Jonathan arose”; NASB keeps “rose up.”
“He said” is rendered “he thought,” and the repeated “not clean” is rendered “he is not clean, surely he is not clean.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the food” is rendered “the meal.”
“Certainly asked” is rendered “earnestly asked leave.”
NASB supplies “to attend.”
“Son of a perverse woman of rebelliousness” is rendered “son of a perverse, rebellious woman!”
